A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same positional-attention research and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Their equations, figures, tables, and experiments can be reliably matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D report original experimental results on numeric algorithms, k-hop induction heads, and mixed-type input tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a value-projection fine-tuning study in Appendix D.1.8 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The architecture in Section 4 remains unchanged, but Appendix D.1.8 adds a limited adaptation procedure: updating only V projection matrices while freezing all other pretrained parameters.

E1.justification: The numeric, induction-head, and mixed-type task coverage is retained. The new fine-tuning study uses three existing numeric tasks and the 10× value domain already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: Standard Transformer variants, GCN, GAT, and GPT2-large remain in their corresponding comparisons. The new fine-tuning experiment reuses the standard Transformer comparator without adding another comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1.8 adds a protocol with 20 fine-tuning epochs on 10× data following the existing 2000-epoch training. Its table reports MSE normalized by the scale factor. Previously reported experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: The new study tests whether adapting only value projections can recover performance under numeric distribution shift, across cumulative sum, cumulative minimum, and sorting. Existing architectural ablations, positional-encoding comparisons, and attention-map analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing plots retain medians and 10th–90th percentile bands over ten runs. The added table reports median MSE, an existing reporting practice, without introducing new run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports ID, 10× OOD, and post-fine-tuning results for three tasks. For example, post-fine-tuning sorting MSE is 1.23e-04 for positional and 6.90e-02 for standard Transformers under the stated normalization. Earlier plotted results and the GCN/GAT table values are retained.

T1.justification: Theorems 5.1 and 6.1 and the mathematical arguments in Appendices A–C, E, and G are retained. Changes to norm expressions, matrix notation, and equation layout do not introduce new assumptions, bounds, or proof arguments.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claim of simulating MPC with O(log n) layers to simulating a single MPC round with that depth. This limited correction aligns the contribution summary with the unchanged round-dependent Theorem 5.1. The abstract and other central contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1.8 newly interprets value-only fine-tuning as a potential efficient adaptation strategy that restores approximately ID-level relative accuracy for positional Transformers. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations concerning input length and OOD theory remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new fine-tuning recipe, including frozen parameters, 20 adaptation epochs, the 10× data scale, and MSE normalization, with references to the retained pretraining setup. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands its context with combinatorial-optimization and broader algorithmic-learning literature, including Vinyals et al. (2015), Butoi et al. (2025), and Barbero et al. (2025). The closest-prior-work comparisons and central novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Appendix D subsection outline, expands the related-work paragraph, and makes localized wording, heading, and example-formatting edits. The main narrative and overall appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the fine-tuning table, renumbers the retained GCN/GAT table, enlarges several existing plots, and reformats equations. Figures are relocated, including experimental plots that now interrupt Appendix E's derivation, while their underlying visual content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new controlled fine-tuning study supplies useful evidence about adaptation that v2 lacked, while the per-round expressivity correction improves precision. These limited evidential and clarity gains outweigh some less convenient figure placement. The core theory and original benchmark evidence remain stable.
